title: The Future
description: The future active and middle indicative, the future of stems ending in a consonant, and verbs with a deponent future.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: The future is made on the future stem: the verb stem plus σ (λυ- + σ = λυσ-), with the primary endings joined by the variable vowel. A labial (π, β, φ) and σ make ψ (πέμψω); a palatal (κ, γ, χ) and σ make ξ (ἄξω, διώξω); a dental (τ, δ, θ) drops before σ (πείσω, δοξάσω). Many verbs have a different stem in the present: κηρύσσω has κηρυκ-, future κηρύξω; διδάσκω has διδαχ-, future διδάξω. Learn each verb's future with the verb.

blocks.caption: λύσομαι, I shall loose for myself
Deponent futures
blocks.html: Some verbs that are active in the present have a middle future with an active meaning: γινώσκω, γνώσομαι; λαμβάνω, λήμψομαι; βαίνω, βήσομαι; and ἔρχομαι has ἐλεύσομαι, γίνομαι has γενήσομαι. ἔχω has the future ἕξω, with a rough breathing.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: λύσεις (you will loose) and λύεις (you loose) differ only by σ; λύσει (he will loose) and λύσῃ (you will loose for yourself) differ in the last vowel.
